terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js reads, creates, updates and deletes a boat through your API.

tasks.title: Keep the fleet in memory
tasks.description:
Implement `createBoatStore(seed)` in `src/store.js`. It keeps boats in a `Map` keyed by `code`, starting from a copy of `seed`, and returns an object with five methods:

- `list()` returns every boat, in the order they were added
- `get(code)` returns the boat, or `undefined`
- `create(boat)` adds it and returns it; a code that already exists throws `new HttpError(409, 'conflict', message)`
- `update(code, changes)` merges `changes` into the boat and returns the whole boat, or returns `undefined` when there is none; the code never changes, even if `changes` has one
- `remove(code)` deletes the boat and returns `true`, or returns `false` when there is none

Boats go in and come out as **copies**: changing an object you passed in or got back must never change what the store holds. The check runs each method on a fresh store, including two stores made from the same seed array.
nextSteps: Build the Map from the seed, one entry per boat.
Write `list` and `get` first, then `create` with its duplicate check.
Write `update` and `remove`, using what `Map` already returns.
Make every way in and out a copy, then press Check.
hints: A Map remembers the order keys were added, and `has`, `get`, `set` and `delete` cover almost everything here.
Objects are shared by reference. If the store keeps the same object it hands out, a caller can change the store without asking. A spread like `{ ...boat }` makes a shallow copy.
For update, spread the old boat, then the changes, then put the original `code` back last. `map.delete(code)` already returns true or false.

tasks.title: Create and read boats
tasks.description:
Fill in `getBoat` and `createBoat` in `src/app.js`. Each handler gets `(req, res, { store, params })`, where `params.code` comes from the `:code` in the path.

- `GET /boats/:code` answers `200` with the boat, or `404` with code `not_found`
- `POST /boats` reads the body with `readJson`, checks it with `validateBoat`, stores it and answers `201` with the stored boat and a `location` header such as `/boats/TW-09`
- a code that already exists answers `409` with code `conflict`

Throw an `HttpError` for every error answer; `createApp` turns it into JSON. The check starts your app with its own seed of three boats.
nextSteps: Set the `location` header before you send the 201.
Run `node try.js` and read the first three answers.
hints: Each handler is a few lines. The store and validateBoat already do the hard parts.
The 409 comes from the store. If you let its HttpError bubble up, createApp sends it for you.
In createBoat: `const boat = store.create(validateBoat(await readJson(req)))`, then `res.setHeader('location', ...)` and `sendJson(res, 201, boat)`.

tasks.title: Change and retire boats
tasks.description:
Fill in `updateBoat` and `deleteBoat` in `src/app.js`.

- `PATCH /boats/:code` checks the body with `validateBoat(input, { partial: true })`, merges it with `store.update` and answers `200` with the whole updated boat
- `DELETE /boats/:code` removes the boat and answers `204` with **no body**
- both answer `404` with code `not_found` when there is no such boat

Partial mode lets every field be optional and refuses a new `code`. The check patches, deletes and then reads the fleet back.
nextSteps: Write `updateBoat` the same way as `createBoat`, but with partial validation.
Turn an `undefined` from the store into a 404.
Write `deleteBoat` so it sends a status with no body.
Run `node try.js` and read the last three answers.
hints: PATCH sends only what changes. PUT would replace the whole thing, which is not what the booking page wants.
204 means there is no body at all, so `sendJson` is the wrong tool here.
For delete, `if (!store.remove(params.code)) throw boatNotFound(params.code)`, then `res.writeHead(204)` and `res.end()`.
